Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines.             ii_low.append(l)

def permutation_test(ii_high, ii_low, B=10000, seed=42):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    obs = np.median(ii_low) - np.median(ii_high)
    pooled = np.concatenate([ii_high, ii_low])
    n_h = len(ii_high)
    count = 0
    for _ in range(B):
        rng.shuffle(pooled)
        d = np.median(pooled[n_h:]) - np.median(pooled[:n_h])
        if abs(d) >= abs(obs):
            count += 1

def bootstrap_ci(ii_high, ii_low, B=10000, seed=42):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    n = min(len(ii_high), len(ii_low))

    for i in range(B):

            n_none = sum(1 for v in vals if v is None)
            n_nan = sum(1 for v in vals if isinstance(v, float) and math.isnan(v))
            n_inf = sum(1 for v in vals if isinstance(v, float) and math.isinf(v))
            if n_none > 0:
                issues.append(f"{prefix} {field}: {n_none} null values")
            if n_nan > 0:
                issues.append(f"{prefix} {field}: {n_nan} NaN values")
            if n_inf > 0:
                issues.append(f"{prefix} {field}: {n_inf} Inf values")

        for field in seg_fields:

def validate_cross_condition_alignment(dirs_and_data):
    """Check that paired conditions share the same problem_ids in the same order."""
    issues = []
    pid_sets = {}
    for dirname, data in dirs_and_data.items():
        if data is None:
            continue
        ppi = data.get("per_problem_ii", {})
        for sk, problems in ppi.items():
            pids = tuple(p.get("problem_id") for p in problems)
            pid_sets[dirname] = pids

    names = list(pid_sets.keys())
    if len(names) < 2:
        return issues

    ref_name = names[0]
    ref_pids = pid_sets[ref_name]
    for name in names[1:]:
        other_pids = pid_sets[name]
        if len(ref_pids) != len(other_pids):
            issues.append(f"Problem count mismatch: {ref_name} has {len(ref_pids)}, {name} has {len(other_pids)}")
        elif ref_pids != other_pids:
            mismatches = sum(1 for a, b in zip(ref_pids, other_pids) if a != b)
            issues.append(f"Problem order mismatch between {ref_name} and {name}: {mismatches} positions differ")

    return issues
